records.source: וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר־יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר׃
records.gloss: And came [the] word of Yahweh to me, saying:
pieces: The word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to me:

L.1: The word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to me, saying:

decisions.choice: the chapter: the ruler of Tyre, a lament over its king, Sidon, and a promise to Israel
decisions.reason: Verses 2-10 condemn the ruler of Tyre for claiming to be a god. Verses 11-19 are a lament over the king of Tyre, pictured in the garden of Eden. Verses 20-23 are a short oracle against Sidon, and verses 24-26 close the oracles against Israel's neighbors with a promise to Israel.

decisions.choice: The word of the LORD came to me, saying (L); came to me (B); The LORD gave me this message (R)
decisions.reason: The settled formula, as in 1:3.

records.heading: The ruler who said, I am a god

records.source: בֶּן־אָדָ֡ם אֱמֹר֩ לִנְגִ֨יד צֹ֜ר כֹּֽה־אָמַ֣ר׀אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהֹוִ֗ה יַ֣עַן גָּבַ֤הּ לִבְּךָ֙ וַתֹּ֨אמֶר֙ אֵ֣ל אָ֔נִי מוֹשַׁ֧ב אֱלֹהִ֛ים יָשַׁ֖בְתִּי בְּלֵ֣ב יַמִּ֑ים וְאַתָּ֤ה אָדָם֙ וְֽלֹא־אֵ֔ל וַתִּתֵּ֥ן לִבְּךָ֖ כְּלֵ֥ב אֱלֹהִֽים׃
records.gloss: Son of man, say to [the] ruler of Tyre, Thus says [the] Lord Yahweh: Because your heart is proud, and you have said, A god [am] I; [the] seat of gods I sit [in], in [the] heart of [the] seas; but you [are] a human and not a god, and you have made your heart like [the] heart of a god,
pieces: Son of man, say to the prince of Tyre, The Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says this: You are proud at heart, and you have claimed, "I am a god! I sit on the throne of the gods in the heart of the seas." Yet you are a mortal and not a god, though you count your mind equal to the mind of a god.

L.2: Son of man, say to the prince of Tyre, Thus says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}: Because your heart is proud, and you have said, "A god [am] I; [in] the seat of gods I sit, in the heart of the seas," yet you [are] a mortal and not a god, though you have made your heart like the heart of a god,

R.2: Son of man, say to the ruler of Tyre, This is what the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says: You are proud. You have said, "I am a god. I sit on the throne of the gods in the middle of the sea." But you are only a human being, not a god, even though you think you are as wise as a god.

decisions.choice: son of man: a mortal, as God addresses Ezekiel
decisions.reason: See the note at 2:1.

decisions.choice: the prince of Tyre: the ruler of Tyre, its king
decisions.reason: The word (*nagid*) means a leader or ruler. Verse 12 calls the same ruler "the king of Tyre". The king of Tyre in Ezekiel's day was Ittobaal III (stated from general knowledge); the oracle does not name him, and speaks to the office as much as to the man.

decisions.choice: I am a god; I sit in the seat of gods: the ruler claims divine rank
decisions.reason: Kings in the ancient world often claimed to be divine or to sit among the gods. Tyre's island throne, "in the heart of the seas", seemed out of reach of any enemy. The LORD answers that he is a mortal, a claim tested in verse 9 when his killer stands before him.

decisions.choice: the seat of gods: a divine throne
decisions.reason: The word for "gods" (*elohim*) can also mean God. The ruler claims a seat among the gods, or the very seat of God.

decisions.choice: you have made your heart like the heart of a god: you think yourself as wise as a god
decisions.reason: In Hebrew the heart is the mind and will. He counts his own understanding divine (verses 3-5).

decisions.choice: a mortal (L, B); only a human being (R)
decisions.reason: *'Adam* set against God follows the settled wording ("mortal" / "human beings"). It refers to one man here, so it takes no gender setting. *Nagid* is "prince" at Literal and Balanced and "ruler" at Readable, matching the wording for *nasi'*.

decisions.choice: Thus says the Lord GOD (L); The Lord GOD says this (B); This is what the Lord GOD says (R)
decisions.reason: The settled formula. The LORD's words take no quotation marks; human speech quoted inside them takes double quotes.

records.source: הִנֵּ֥ה חָכָ֛ם אַתָּ֖ה מִדָּֽנִיֵּ֑אלכָּל־סָת֖וּם לֹ֥א עֲמָמֽוּךָ׃
records.gloss: Look, wise [are] you, more than Daniel; nothing hidden is dark to you;
pieces: You are indeed wiser than Daniel; no secret is hidden from you!

L.3: look, you [are] wiser than Daniel; no secret is hidden from you;

R.3: You think you are wiser than Daniel, and that no secret can be kept from you.

decisions.choice: Daniel: the ancient wise man Danel, or the Daniel of the book
decisions.reason: See the note at 14:14. The written Hebrew again spells the name Dan'el. The famous wise man of old fits a saying addressed to a Phoenician king.

decisions.choice: you are wiser than Daniel: said with irony
decisions.reason: The LORD repeats the ruler's own high opinion of himself, in order to bring it down.

decisions.choice: no secret is hidden from you
decisions.reason: The verb is rare and seems to mean "be dark to" or "be a match for". No secret is beyond him.

decisions.choice: You think you are
decisions.reason: Readable makes the irony plain (m2).

records.source: בְּחָכְמָֽתְךָ֙ וּבִתְבוּנָ֣תְךָ֔ עָשִׂ֥יתָ לְּךָ֖ חָ֑יִל וַתַּ֛עַשׂ זָהָ֥ב וָכֶ֖סֶף בְּאוֹצְרוֹתֶֽיךָ׃
records.gloss: by your wisdom and by your understanding you have made for yourself wealth, and you have made gold and silver in your treasuries;
pieces: By your wisdom and understanding you have won wealth for yourself and filled your treasuries with gold and silver.

L.4: by your wisdom and by your understanding you have made wealth for yourself, and you have gathered gold and silver into your treasuries;

R.4: You used your wisdom and skill to make yourself rich. You filled your storerooms with gold and silver.

decisions.choice: wisdom and understanding: skill in business and statecraft
decisions.reason: Here wisdom is practical skill, the cleverness that made Tyre rich through trade (verse 5).

records.source: בְּרֹ֧ב חָכְמָתְךָ֛ בִּרְכֻלָּתְךָ֖ הִרְבִּ֣יתָ חֵילֶ֑ךָ וַיִּגְבַּ֥הּ לְבָבְךָ֖ בְּחֵילֶֽךָ׃ס
records.gloss: by [the] greatness of your wisdom in your trade you have increased your wealth, and your heart has become proud in your wealth.
pieces: By your great skill in trading you have multiplied your wealth, and your wealth has made your heart proud.

L.5: by the greatness of your wisdom in your trade you have increased your wealth, and your heart has become proud because of your wealth.

R.5: You were so good at trading that you became richer and richer. And because you were rich, you became proud.

decisions.choice: your heart has become proud because of your wealth
decisions.reason: Riches lead to pride and to forgetting God (Deuteronomy 8:13-14; Hosea 13:6). Verses 3-5 explain how the ruler came to say "I am a god" (verse 2).

records.source: לָכֵ֕ן כֹּ֥ה אָמַ֖ר אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֑ה יַ֛עַן תִּתְּךָ֥ אֶת־לְבָבְךָ֖ כְּלֵ֥ב אֱלֹהִֽים׃
records.gloss: therefore thus says [the] Lord Yahweh: Because you have made your heart like [the] heart of a god,
pieces: Therefore the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says this: Because you count your mind equal to the mind of a god,

L.6: therefore thus says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}: Because you have made your heart like the heart of a god,

R.6: So this is what the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says: You think you are as wise as a god.

decisions.choice: because ...: the charge of verse 2 repeated
decisions.reason: After the aside of verses 3-5 the LORD takes up the charge again before giving the sentence in verse 7.

decisions.choice: Thus says the Lord GOD (L); The Lord GOD says this (B); This is what the Lord GOD says (R)
decisions.reason: The settled formula. The LORD's words take no quotation marks; human speech quoted inside them takes double quotes.

records.heading: A mortal and not a god

records.source: לָכֵ֗ן הִנְנִ֨י מֵבִ֤יא עָלֶ֨יךָ֙ זָרִ֔ים עָרִיצֵ֖י גּוֹיִ֑ם וְהֵרִ֤יקוּ חַרְבוֹתָם֙ עַל־יְפִ֣י חָכְמָתֶ֔ךָ וְחִלְּל֖וּ יִפְעָתֶֽךָ׃
records.gloss: therefore, look, I [am] about to bring upon you strangers, [the] ruthless of [the] nations, and they will draw their swords against [the] beauty of your wisdom, and they will profane your splendor.
pieces: therefore I am bringing foreigners against you, the most ruthless of nations. They will bare their swords against all that your wisdom made beautiful, and they will defile your splendor.

L.7: therefore, look, I am bringing strangers upon you, the most ruthless of the nations, and they will unsheathe their swords against the beauty of your wisdom and profane your splendor.

R.7: So I am going to bring foreigners to attack you, from the cruelest nation of all. They will draw their swords against all the beautiful things your wisdom has won, and they will ruin your splendor.

decisions.choice: the most ruthless of the nations: Babylon
decisions.reason: Ezekiel uses the same words of the Babylonian armies in 30:11, 31:12 and 32:12.

decisions.choice: profane your splendor: treat as common what claimed to be holy
decisions.reason: The verb means to make something holy common or unclean. The "god" of Tyre will be shown to be no god at all.

decisions.choice: all the beautiful things your wisdom has won
decisions.reason: Readable says what "the beauty of your wisdom" is (verses 4-5).

records.source: לַשַּׁ֖חַת יֽוֹרִד֑וּךָ וָמַ֛תָּה מְמוֹתֵ֥י חָלָ֖ל בְּלֵ֥ב יַמִּֽים׃
records.gloss: To [the] pit they will bring you down, and you will die [the] deaths of [the] slain in [the] heart of [the] seas.
pieces: They will thrust you down into the pit, and you will be slain and die in the heart of the seas.

L.8: To the pit they will bring you down, and you will die the deaths of the slain in the heart of the seas.

R.8: They will send you down to the pit, the world of the dead. You will die a violent death out in the sea.

decisions.choice: the pit: the world of the dead
the deaths of the slain: a violent death
decisions.reason: The plural "deaths" makes the phrase stronger. He will die as those killed in battle die.

decisions.choice: in the heart of the seas: the throne becomes the grave
decisions.reason: He said "I sit in the heart of the seas" (verse 2). There he will die.

records.source: הֶאָמֹ֤ר תֹּאמַר֙ אֱלֹהִ֣ים אָ֔נִי לִפְנֵ֖י הֹֽרְגֶ֑ךָ וְאַתָּ֥ה אָדָ֛ם וְלֹא־אֵ֖ל בְּיַ֥ד מְחַלְלֶֽיךָ׃
records.gloss: Will you really say, A god [am] I, before [the one who] kills you? And you [are] a human and not a god in [the] hand of [those who] pierce you.
pieces: Will you still say, "I am a god," when you face the one who kills you? You will be only a mortal, not a god, in the hands of those who strike you down.

L.9: Will you really say, "A god [am] I," before the one who kills you? You [are] a mortal and not a god in the hand of those who pierce you.

R.9: When your killer stands in front of you, will you still say, "I am a god"? No, you will be only a human being, not a god, when they kill you.

decisions.choice: the test of the claim: a god does not die at a man's hand
decisions.reason: The question exposes the boast of verse 2. Facing death, the ruler will be seen as a mortal.

decisions.choice: those who pierce you: the verb echoes "profane" in verse 7
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word for "pierce" here has the same consonants as "profane". Those who profane his splendor are the ones who run him through.

records.source: מוֹתֵ֧י עֲרֵלִ֛ים תָּמ֖וּת בְּיַד־זָרִ֑ים כִּ֚י אֲנִ֣י דִבַּ֔רְתִּי נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה׃ס
records.gloss: [The] deaths of [the] uncircumcised you will die by [the] hand of strangers, for I have spoken, declaration of [the] Lord Yahweh.
pieces: At the hands of foreigners you will die the death of the uncircumcised, for I have spoken, declares the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}.

L.10: The deaths of the uncircumcised you will die by the hand of strangers, for I have spoken, declares the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}.

R.10: You will die in disgrace, as the uncircumcised die, killed by foreigners. I have spoken, says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: the deaths of the uncircumcised: a shameful death
decisions.reason: To die "uncircumcised" was to die in disgrace, outside the honored dead. The Phoenicians may themselves have practiced circumcision (stated from general knowledge), which would make the phrase sharper. Ezekiel uses it again of Pharaoh and the nations in the world of the dead (31:18; 32:19-32).

decisions.choice: in disgrace
decisions.reason: Readable says what dying "the deaths of the uncircumcised" meant (m1).

decisions.choice: declares the Lord GOD (L, B); says the Lord GOD (R)
decisions.reason: The settled wording for *ne'um Adonai YHWH* in Ezekiel.

records.source: וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר־יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר׃
records.gloss: And came [the] word of Yahweh to me, saying:
pieces: Then the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to me:

L.11: Then the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to me, saying:

R.11: Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gave me this message:

decisions.choice: the word of the LORD came to me (all levels, as verse 1)
decisions.reason: The settled formula, with "Then" because a second message follows the first.

records.heading: A lament for the king of Tyre

records.source: בֶּן־אָדָ֕ם שָׂ֥א קִינָ֖ה עַל־מֶ֣לֶךְ צ֑וֹר וְאָמַ֣רְתָּ לּ֗וֹ כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה אַתָּה֙ חוֹתֵ֣ם תָּכְנִ֔ית מָלֵ֥א חָכְמָ֖ה וּכְלִ֥יל יֹֽפִי׃
records.gloss: Son of man, take up a lament over [the] king of Tyre, and say to him, Thus says [the] Lord Yahweh: You [were] a sealer of a pattern, full of wisdom and perfect of beauty.
pieces: Son of man, raise a lament over the king of Tyre \q and say to him, The Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says this: \q You were the model of perfection, \q full of wisdom and perfect in beauty.

L.12: Son of man, take up a lament over the king of Tyre, \q and say to him, Thus says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}: \q You [were] the seal of the pattern, \q full of wisdom and perfect in beauty.

R.12: Son of man, sing a funeral song about the king of Tyre. \q Say to him, This is what the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says: \q You were a perfect example, \q full of wisdom and perfectly beautiful.

decisions.choice: son of man: a mortal, as God addresses Ezekiel
decisions.reason: See the note at 2:1.

decisions.choice: a lament over the king of Tyre
decisions.reason: See the note at 19:1. Verses 12-19 are a lament, set in lines as poetry. It tells the king's story as a story of Eden: created perfect, placed in the garden of God, then cast out for his pride and destroyed.

decisions.choice: the king of Tyre in Eden: the text addresses the king; the reading of Satan's fall is later
decisions.reason: The lament speaks to "the king of Tyre", and its charges are his: his wealth and trade (verses 16, 18) and his pride in his beauty and wisdom (verse 17), the same charges as in verses 2-10. To show how far he will fall, it pictures him in the garden of God, like the first man, and as a cherub on God's mountain. From early times some Christian writers read the passage, with Isaiah 14:12-15, as a picture of the fall of Satan, an angel who fell through pride (stated from general knowledge). That reading comes later than the text, which nowhere names Satan or an angel and addresses a human ruler, as Isaiah 14 addresses the king of Babylon (Isaiah 14:4, 16). The wording here translates what the lament says to the king and is not shaped to the later reading.

decisions.choice: the seal of the pattern: the model of perfection
decisions.reason: The phrase is obscure. A seal bore a design and stamped it; "seal of a pattern" seems to mean the finished model, the sum of perfection. It may also mean "sealing (completing) the measure".

decisions.choice: no quotation marks; set in lines; funeral song (R)
decisions.reason: The lament is what Ezekiel is told to say, so it takes no quotation marks under the quotation rule for Ezekiel. The lines follow the Hebrew accents. Readable says "funeral song" for *qinah*, as in 19:1.

records.source: בְּעֵ֨דֶן גַּן־אֱלֹהִ֜ים הָיִ֗יתָ כָּל־אֶ֨בֶן יְקָרָ֤ה מְסֻכָתֶ֨ךָ֙ אֹ֣דֶם פִּטְדָ֞ה וְיָהֲלֹ֗ם תַּרְשִׁ֥ישׁ שֹׁ֨הַם֙ וְיָ֣שְׁפֵ֔ה סַפִּ֣יר נֹ֔פֶךְ וּבָרְקַ֖ת וְזָהָ֑ב מְלֶ֨אכֶת תֻּפֶּ֤יךָ וּנְקָבֶ֨יךָ֙ בָּ֔ךְ בְּי֥וֹם הִבָּרַאֲךָ֖ כּוֹנָֽנוּ׃
records.gloss: In Eden, [the] garden of God, you were; every precious stone [was] your covering: carnelian, topaz and emerald, chrysolite, onyx and jasper, sapphire, turquoise and beryl, and gold; [the] workmanship of your settings and your sockets [was] in you; on [the] day you were created they were prepared.
pieces: You were in Eden, the garden of God; you were clothed in every precious stone: carnelian, topaz and emerald, chrysolite, onyx and jasper, \q sapphire, turquoise and beryl, and gold. \q Your settings and mountings were crafted for you; \q on the day you were created they were made ready.

L.13: In Eden, the garden of God, you were; every precious stone [was] your covering: carnelian, topaz and emerald, chrysolite, onyx and jasper, \q sapphire, turquoise and beryl, and gold; \q the workmanship of your settings and your sockets [was] in you; \q on the day you were created they were prepared.

R.13: You were in Eden, the garden of God. You were covered with every kind of precious stone: carnelian, topaz, emerald, chrysolite, onyx, jasper, \q sapphire, turquoise, beryl and gold. \q Beautiful settings were made for your jewels. \q They were made ready on the day you were created.

decisions.choice: Eden, the garden of God: the king pictured as the first man
decisions.reason: Eden is the garden where God placed the first human being (Genesis 2:8-15). Ezekiel calls it "the garden of God" again in 31:8-9 and 36:35. Genesis 2:12 also speaks of gold and precious stone in the land around Eden.

decisions.choice: nine precious stones: nine of the twelve on the high priest's breastpiece
decisions.reason: Each of the nine stones is one of the twelve set on the breastpiece of the high priest (Exodus 28:17-20), though in a different order, and the picture may cast the king as a priestly figure in God's garden. The Greek translation lists all twelve stones, with silver and gold (stated from general knowledge). The names of ancient gems are hard to match with modern ones.

decisions.choice: your settings and your sockets: the jeweler's work
decisions.reason: The first word usually means a tambourine and the second a hole or socket. Here they seem to be terms of the jeweler's craft, the mountings in which the stones were set. Other readings are possible.

decisions.choice: on the day you were created
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used for God's creating in Genesis 1:1, 27. The king is spoken of as a creature made by God, as in verse 15.

decisions.choice: carnelian, topaz, emerald, chrysolite, onyx, jasper, sapphire, turquoise, beryl
decisions.reason: The names of the stones follow Exodus 28:17-20 at each level, so that the reader can see that they are the same stones.

records.source: אַ֨תְּ־כְּר֔וּב מִמְשַׁ֖ח הַסּוֹכֵ֑ךְ וּנְתַתִּ֗יךָ בְּהַ֨ר קֹ֤דֶשׁ אֱלֹהִים֙ הָיִ֔יתָ בְּת֥וֹךְ אַבְנֵי־אֵ֖שׁ הִתְהַלָּֽכְתָּ׃
records.gloss: You [were a] cherub, anointed, the covering [one], and I placed you; on [the] holy mountain of God you were; in [the] midst of stones of fire you walked about.
pieces: You were an anointed guardian cherub; \q I placed you there. You were on God's holy mountain; \q you walked among the stones of fire.

L.14: You [were] an anointed cherub, the guardian, \q and I placed you [there]; on the holy mountain of God you were; \q in the midst of stones of fire you walked about.

R.14: You were a guardian cherub, anointed for your task. \q I put you on God's holy mountain. \q You walked among the fiery stones.

decisions.choice: a guardian cherub: a winged being who guards God's presence
decisions.reason: Cherubim guarded the way to the tree of life in Eden (Genesis 3:24), and the golden cherubim on the ark spread their wings to cover it (Exodus 25:20, where the same verb, "cover", is used). See the note on cherubim at 10:1.

decisions.choice: you were a cherub
alternatives: with the cherub I placed you
decisions.reason: The Hebrew reads "you (were) a cherub". The Greek translation, with different vowels, reads "with the cherub I placed you", so that the king is the man in the garden and the cherub is beside him; in verse 16 the Greek has the cherub drive him out (stated from general knowledge). The Hebrew is kept: the king is pictured as the guardian cherub himself.

decisions.choice: anointed
decisions.reason: The word occurs only here. It may mean "anointed", set apart for a task, or come from a root meaning "spread out", picturing the cherub's outspread wings.

decisions.choice: the holy mountain of God, the stones of fire
decisions.reason: Eden is pictured as a mountain, the dwelling of God, as Zion is God's holy mountain (20:40). The "stones of fire" may be the flashing gems of verse 13 or the fiery brightness around God (1:13; Exodus 24:10, 17).

decisions.choice: cherub, at every level
decisions.reason: Every level keeps "cherub", as chapter 10 does. The words are said to the king of Tyre (see the note at verse 12).

records.source: תָּמִ֤ים אַתָּה֙ בִּדְרָכֶ֔יךָ מִיּ֖וֹם הִבָּֽרְאָ֑ךְ עַד־נִמְצָ֥א עַוְלָ֖תָה בָּֽךְ׃
records.gloss: Blameless [were] you in your ways from [the] day you were created until was found unrighteousness in you.
pieces: You were blameless in your ways \q from the day you were created, \q until wickedness was found in you.

L.15: Blameless [were] you in your ways \q from the day you were created, \q until unrighteousness was found in you.

R.15: You did what was right in every way \q from the day you were created \q until evil was found in you.

decisions.choice: blameless: whole, without fault
decisions.reason: The word is used of Noah and of the life God asks of Abraham (Genesis 6:9; 17:1).

decisions.choice: until unrighteousness was found in you: the fall
decisions.reason: Like the first human beings, the king began well and fell. Verses 16-18 name the wrong: violence and dishonesty in trade, and pride.

records.source: בְּרֹ֣ב רְכֻלָּתְךָ֗ מָל֧וּ תוֹכְךָ֛ חָמָ֖ס וַֽתֶּחֱטָ֑א וָאֶחַלֶּלְךָ֩ מֵהַ֨ר אֱלֹהִ֤ים וָֽאַבֶּדְךָ֙ כְּר֣וּב הַסֹּכֵ֔ךְ מִתּ֖וֹךְ אַבְנֵי־אֵֽשׁ׃
records.gloss: In [the] abundance of your trade they filled your midst [with] violence, and you sinned; and I cast you as profane from [the] mountain of God, and I destroyed you, cherub, the covering [one], from [the] midst of [the] stones of fire.
pieces: Through your vast trade you were filled with violence, and you sinned. \q So I threw you in disgrace from the mountain of God, and I destroyed you, guardian cherub, \q removing you from among the stones of fire.

L.16: In the abundance of your trade your midst was filled with violence, and you sinned; \q so I cast you as profane from the mountain of God, and I destroyed you, guardian cherub, \q from the midst of the stones of fire.

R.16: You traded so much that you became full of violence, and you sinned. \q So I threw you off the mountain of God in disgrace. I destroyed you, guardian cherub, \q and took you away from the fiery stones.

decisions.choice: trade filled with violence: wealth gained by oppression
decisions.reason: Tyre's trade, which made it great (chapter 27), became violent and unjust: gain at the expense of others, including the slave trade (27:13; Amos 1:9).

decisions.choice: I cast you as profane from the mountain of God
decisions.reason: What is profane cannot stay in a holy place. The king is thrown out as unclean, as the man and woman were sent out of the garden (Genesis 3:23-24).

decisions.choice: and I destroyed you, guardian cherub
alternatives: and the guardian cherub drove you out
decisions.reason: The Greek translation reads "and the cherub drove you out" (stated from general knowledge); see verse 14.

records.source: גָּבַ֤הּ לִבְּךָ֙ בְּיָפְיֶ֔ךָ שִׁחַ֥תָּ חָכְמָתְךָ֖ עַל־יִפְעָתֶ֑ךָ עַל־אֶ֣רֶץ הִשְׁלַכְתִּ֗יךָ לִפְנֵ֧י מְלָכִ֛ים נְתַתִּ֖יךָ לְרַ֥אֲוָה בָֽךְ׃
records.gloss: Was proud your heart in your beauty; you corrupted your wisdom on account of your splendor; on [the] ground I threw you; before kings I put you, to look at you.
pieces: Your heart grew proud because of your beauty; \q you corrupted your wisdom for the sake of your splendor. \q I threw you to the ground; I made you a spectacle before kings.

L.17: Your heart was proud because of your beauty; \q you corrupted your wisdom for the sake of your splendor; \q to the ground I cast you; before kings I set you, to look at you.

R.17: You became proud because you were so beautiful. \q You spoiled your wisdom because you loved your own splendor. \q So I threw you down to the ground. I made you a sight for kings to stare at.

decisions.choice: pride in beauty and splendor: the root of the fall
decisions.reason: The charge matches verses 2-5: the king's gifts turned into pride (Proverbs 16:18).

decisions.choice: before kings I set you, to look at you: a public disgrace
decisions.reason: The fallen king is put on show, so that other kings may see him and take warning.

records.source: מֵרֹ֣ב עֲוֺנֶ֗יךָ בְּעֶ֨וֶל֙ רְכֻלָּ֣תְךָ֔ חִלַּ֖לְתָּ מִקְדָּשֶׁ֑יךָ וָֽאוֹצִא־אֵ֤שׁ מִתּֽוֹכְךָ֙ הִ֣יא אֲכָלַ֔תְךָ וָאֶתֶּנְךָ֤ לְאֵ֨פֶר֙ עַל־הָאָ֔רֶץ לְעֵינֵ֖י כָּל־רֹאֶֽיךָ׃
records.gloss: By [the] multitude of your iniquities, in [the] unrighteousness of your trade, you profaned your sanctuaries; and I brought out fire from your midst; it has consumed you, and I have made you ashes on the earth in [the] eyes of all who see you.
pieces: By your many sins, by the dishonesty of your trade, \q you defiled your sanctuaries. \q So I brought fire out from within you, and it devoured you; \q I turned you to ashes on the ground \q in the sight of all who were watching.

L.18: By the multitude of your iniquities, in the unrighteousness of your trade, \q you profaned your sanctuaries; \q so I brought fire out from your midst; it has consumed you, \q and I have made you ashes on the earth \q in the eyes of all who see you.

R.18: You sinned so much and were so dishonest in your trade \q that you made your holy places unclean. \q So I made a fire break out from inside you, and it burned you up. \q I turned you to ashes on the ground \q while everyone watched.

decisions.choice: your sanctuaries: Tyre's temples, or the holy place of the poem
decisions.reason: The king's sins made unclean the holy places he served, Tyre's own temples, or, in the picture of the poem, the holy mountain of God (verses 14, 16).

decisions.choice: fire from your midst: destruction from within
decisions.reason: The fire comes out of the king himself: his own sin destroys him.

decisions.choice: iniquities (L); sins (B, R)
decisions.reason: *'Awon* follows the Isaiah table.

records.source: כָּל־יוֹדְעֶ֨יךָ֙ בָּֽעַמִּ֔ים שָׁמְמ֖וּ עָלֶ֑יךָ בַּלָּה֣וֹת הָיִ֔יתָ וְאֵינְךָ֖ עַד־עוֹלָֽם׃פ
records.gloss: All [who] know you among [the] peoples are appalled over you; sudden terrors you have become, and you will not [be] until perpetuity.
pieces: All among the peoples who knew you \q are appalled at your fate; \q you have come to a terrifying end, \q and you will be no more forever.

L.19: All who know you among the peoples \q are appalled over you; \q sudden terrors you have become, \q and you will be no more forever.

R.19: All the nations who knew you \q are shocked at what happened to you. \q You have come to a horrible end, \q and you will be gone forever.

decisions.choice: the refrain of the Tyre oracles
decisions.reason: The lament ends as 26:21 and 27:36 do.

records.source: וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר־יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר׃
records.gloss: And came [the] word of Yahweh to me, saying:
pieces: Then the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to me:

L.20: Then the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to me, saying:

R.20: Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gave me this message:

decisions.choice: the word of the LORD came to me (all levels, as verse 1)
decisions.reason: The settled formula, with "Then" because a new message follows.

records.heading: Against Sidon

records.source: בֶּן־אָדָ֕ם שִׂ֥ים פָּנֶ֖יךָ אֶל־צִיד֑וֹן וְהִנָּבֵ֖א עָלֶֽיהָ׃
records.gloss: Son of man, set your face toward Sidon, and prophesy against her,
pieces: Son of man, turn to face Sidon and prophesy against her,

L.21: Son of man, set your face toward Sidon, and prophesy against her,

R.21: Son of man, turn toward Sidon. Prophesy against it.

decisions.choice: son of man: a mortal, as God addresses Ezekiel
decisions.reason: See the note at 2:1.

decisions.choice: Sidon: Tyre's sister city to the north
decisions.reason: Sidon was the older Phoenician port, about twenty-five miles north of Tyre (27:8). Its gods, Baal and Astarte, were worshiped in Israel through Jezebel, daughter of a king of the Sidonians (1 Kings 16:31).

decisions.choice: set your face toward (L); turn to face (B); turn toward (R)
decisions.reason: The settled wording; see 6:2. As with Tyre, Literal and Balanced keep "her" for the city and Readable says "it".

records.source: וְאָמַרְתָּ֗ כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה הִנְנִ֤י עָלַ֨יִךְ֙ צִיד֔וֹן וְנִכְבַּדְתִּ֖י בְּתוֹכֵ֑ךְ וְֽיָדְע֞וּ כִּֽי־אֲנִ֣י יְהוָ֗ה בַּעֲשׂ֥וֹתִי בָ֛הּ שְׁפָטִ֖ים וְנִקְדַּ֥שְׁתִּי בָֽהּ׃
records.gloss: and say, Thus says [the] Lord Yahweh: Look, I [am] against you, Sidon, and I will be glorified in your midst; and they will know that I [am] Yahweh, when I execute in her judgments and show myself holy in her.
pieces: and say, The Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says this: I am against you, Sidon, and I will show {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} glory within you. Then they will know that I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, when I carry out judgments on her and show {{deity_pronoun:myself|Myself}} holy in her.

L.22: and say, Thus says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}: Look, I [am] against you, Sidon, and I will be glorified in your midst; and they will know that I [am] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, when I work judgments in her and show {{deity_pronoun:myself|Myself}} holy in her.

R.22: Say, This is what the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says: Sidon, I am against you. I will show {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} glory in you. Then people will know that I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, when I punish Sidon and show that I am holy.

decisions.choice: I will be glorified ... show myself holy: the LORD makes himself known through judgment
decisions.reason: When the LORD acts, his honor and his holiness are seen by all (Exodus 14:4; Leviticus 10:3; Ezekiel 20:41; 38:16).

decisions.choice: in her: the oracle turns from speaking to Sidon to speaking about it
decisions.reason: The change of person is common in the prophets.

decisions.choice: Thus says the Lord GOD (L); The Lord GOD says this (B); This is what the Lord GOD says (R)
decisions.reason: The settled formula. The LORD's words take no quotation marks; human speech quoted inside them takes double quotes.

decisions.choice: and they will know that I am the LORD (L); Then they will know (B, R)
decisions.reason: The refrain follows the settled wording; see 6:7.

records.source: וְשִׁלַּחְתִּי־בָ֞הּ דֶּ֤בֶר וָדָם֙ בְּח֣וּצוֹתֶ֔יהָ וְנִפְלַ֤ל חָלָל֙ בְּתוֹכָ֔הּ בְּחֶ֥רֶב עָלֶ֖יהָ מִסָּבִ֑יב וְיָדְע֖וּ כִּֽי־אֲנִ֥י יְהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: And I will send into her pestilence and blood into her streets, and will fall [the] slain in her midst by [the] sword against her from all around; and they will know that I [am] Yahweh.
pieces: I will send plague into her and bloodshed into her streets. The slain will fall within her, struck by the sword that comes against her from every side. Then they will know that I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.23: And I will send into her pestilence, and blood into her streets, and the slain will fall in her midst by the sword [that is] against her from all around; and they will know that I [am] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.23: I will send disease on Sidon, and blood will flow in its streets. People will be killed inside the city by enemies who attack from every side. Then they will know that I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: pestilence and blood: disease and violent death
decisions.reason: The pair comes in Ezekiel's lists of judgments (5:17; 14:19; 38:22).

decisions.choice: pestilence (L); plague (B); disease (R)
decisions.reason: The settled wording for *deber*.

decisions.choice: and they will know that I am the LORD (L); Then they will know (B, R)
decisions.reason: The refrain follows the settled wording; see 6:7.

records.source: וְלֹֽא־יִהְיֶ֨ה ע֜וֹד לְבֵ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל סִלּ֤וֹן מַמְאִיר֙ וְק֣וֹץ מַכְאִ֔ב מִכֹּל֙ סְבִ֣יבֹתָ֔ם הַשָּׁאטִ֖ים אוֹתָ֑ם וְיָ֣דְע֔וּ כִּ֥י אֲנִ֖י אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה׃ס
records.gloss: And there will not be again for [the] house of Israel a brier pricking and a thorn causing pain from all around them who despise them; and they will know that I [am the] Lord Yahweh.
pieces: The house of Israel will no longer have neighbors who treat them with contempt and hurt them like a pricking brier or a painful thorn. Then they will know that I am the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}.

L.24: And there will no longer be for the house of Israel a pricking brier or a painful thorn from all who are around them, who treat them with contempt; and they will know that I [am] the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}.

R.24: The people of Israel will no longer be surrounded by neighbors who hate them and hurt them like sharp thorns. Then they will know that I am the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: a pricking brier, a painful thorn: troublesome neighbors
decisions.reason: Numbers 33:55 warns that the peoples left in the land would be "thorns in your sides". With the judgments on Ammon, Moab, Edom, the Philistines, Tyre and Sidon, those thorns are removed.

decisions.choice: verses 24-26: the close of the oracles against Israel's neighbors
decisions.reason: The six neighbors of chapters 25-28 have been judged. Before the oracles on Egypt (29-32) the LORD promises Israel peace in its own land.

decisions.choice: and they will know that I am the LORD (L); Then they will know (B, R)
decisions.reason: The refrain follows the settled wording; see 6:7. Here the refrain names "the Lord GOD".

records.source: כֹּֽה־אָמַר֮ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִה֒ בְּקַבְּצִ֣י׀אֶת־בֵּ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל מִן־הָֽעַמִּים֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר נָפֹ֣צוּ בָ֔ם וְנִקְדַּ֥שְׁתִּי בָ֖ם לְעֵינֵ֣י הַגּוֹיִ֑ם וְיָֽשְׁבוּ֙ עַל־אַדְמָתָ֔ם אֲשֶׁ֥ר נָתַ֖תִּי לְעַבְדִּ֥י לְיַעֲקֹֽב׃
records.gloss: Thus says [the] Lord Yahweh: When I gather the house of Israel from the peoples among whom they have been scattered, and I show myself holy among them in [the] eyes of the nations, then they will dwell on their land which I gave to my servant, to Jacob.
pieces: The Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says this: When I gather the house of Israel from the nations where they have been scattered, I will display {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} holiness among them as the nations look on. Then they will live in their own land, the land I gave to {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servant Jacob.

L.25: Thus says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}: When I gather the house of Israel out of the peoples among whom they have been scattered, and show {{deity_pronoun:myself|Myself}} holy among them in the eyes of the nations, then they will dwell on their own land which I gave to {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servant, to Jacob.

R.25: This is what the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says: I will gather the people of Israel from the nations where they have been scattered. Through them I will show the nations that I am holy. Then they will live in their own land, the land I gave to {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servant Jacob.

decisions.choice: the gathering of Israel: the LORD's holiness shown to the nations
decisions.reason: The promise looks ahead to chapters 34-37. Israel's scattering dishonored the LORD's name among the nations; its return will show his holiness (20:41; 36:22-24).

decisions.choice: my servant Jacob: the patriarch, and the people named after him
decisions.reason: The land was promised to Jacob (Genesis 28:13; 35:12). Isaiah and Jeremiah call the people "my servant Jacob" (Isaiah 41:8; Jeremiah 30:10).

decisions.choice: servant, at every level
decisions.reason: The prophets use "servant" for "my servant" at every level (Jeremiah 7:25; Amos 3:7), as the terms note records.

decisions.choice: Thus says the Lord GOD (L); The Lord GOD says this (B); This is what the Lord GOD says (R)
decisions.reason: The settled formula. The LORD's words take no quotation marks; human speech quoted inside them takes double quotes.

records.heading: Israel gathered and safe

records.source: וְיָשְׁב֣וּ עָלֶיהָ֮ לָבֶטַח֒ וּבָנ֤וּ בָתִּים֙ וְנָטְע֣וּ כְרָמִ֔ים וְיָשְׁב֖וּ לָבֶ֑טַח בַּעֲשׂוֹתִ֣י שְׁפָטִ֗ים בְּכֹ֨ל הַשָּׁאטִ֤ים אֹתָם֙ מִסְּבִ֣יבוֹתָ֔ם וְיָ֣דְע֔וּ כִּ֛י אֲנִ֥י יְהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵיהֶֽם׃ס
records.gloss: And they will dwell on it in security, and they will build houses and plant vineyards, and they will dwell in security, when I execute judgments on all [who] despise them from around them; and they will know that I [am] Yahweh their God.
pieces: They will live there in safety; they will build houses and plant vineyards. They will live in safety when I carry out judgments on all their neighbors who despise them. Then they will know that I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} their God.

L.26: And they will dwell on it securely, and build houses and plant vineyards; and they will dwell securely, when I execute judgments on all who treat them with contempt from around them; and they will know that I [am] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} their God.

R.26: They will live there safely. They will build houses and plant vineyards. They will live in safety when I punish all the nations around them that hated them. Then they will know that I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} their God.

decisions.choice: build houses and plant vineyards: a settled, blessed life
decisions.reason: The covenant curse was to build and plant and not enjoy it (Deuteronomy 28:30). The promise reverses it (Isaiah 65:21; Jeremiah 29:5; Amos 9:14).

decisions.choice: securely: without fear of enemies
decisions.reason: Living securely in the land is the blessing promised in Leviticus 25:18-19, and it returns in 34:25-28.

decisions.choice: and they will know that I am the LORD (L); Then they will know (B, R)
decisions.reason: The refrain follows the settled wording; see 6:7.
